The first three sentences are: "Because it makes the timer unnecessary. `allow()` works out how many tokens should have accrued since the last call (`elapsed * rate`) and adds them just before it decides. This is lazy refill, and it gives the same answer a ticking timer would." They describe the mechanism and claim it is equivalent to a timer. Apart from removing the timer itself, they name no concrete thing it gives that a timer does not. Those advantages (cost scales with use, no race on shared state, exact fractional refill) appear only from line 5 onward.
"`api.py` creates one `TokenBucket` per `api_key` in a module-level dict." and "It uses `time.monotonic()`."
